# NanoC language guide

## Hello, NanoC

Save this as `hello.nc`. Lines starting with `#` pass through unchanged, so any C header works.

```nanoc
#include <stdio.h>
@f main int
  puts("Hello from NanoC!")
  0
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    puts("Hello from NanoC!");
    return 0;
}
```

> Build: `nanoc hello.nc -o hello.c && cc hello.c -o hello && ./hello`

## Bare return types

The return type goes after the parameters, with no arrow. Omit it for `void`. Group parameters that share a type with a comma. A one-line body can be an `=` expression.

```nanoc
#include <stdio.h>
@f add(int a,b) int = a+b
@f greet(char *name)
  printf("hi %s\n",name)
@f main int
  greet("NanoC")
  printf("%d\n",add(2,3))
  0
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int add(int a, int b) {
    return a+b;
}

void greet(char *name) {
    printf("hi %s\n",name);
}

int main(void) {
    greet("NanoC");
    printf("%d\n",add(2,3));
    return 0;
}
```

- An indented body returns its final expression. No `return` needed; `ret x` is the short form when you want one.
- No braces, no semicolons, no parentheses around conditions. Parentheses and brackets keep multiline expressions together.

## Blocks produce values

An `if`/`elif`/`else` that covers every branch returns the value of whichever branch runs.

```nanoc
@f sign(int x) int
  if x<0
    -1
  elif x>0
    1
  else
    0
@f main int = sign(-9)!=-1
```

```c
int sign(int x) {
    if (x<0) {
        return -1;
    } else if (x>0) {
        return 1;
    } else {
        return 0;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    return sign(-9)!=-1;
}
```

## Short type names

`i8 i16 i32 i64 u8 u16 u32 u64 f32 f64 byte cstr usize isize` are plain C type words inside NanoC code, so the output builds with any C compiler and needs no extra header (`usize`/`isize` need `stddef.h`). Unmarked C is never rewritten.

```nanoc
#include <stdio.h>
@f add(i32 a,b) i32 = a+b
@f main int
  u8 x=200
  cstr s="hi"
  printf("%s %d\n",s,add(x,2))
  0
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int add(int a, int b) {
    return a+b;
}

int main(void) {
    unsigned char x=200;
    const char * s="hi";
    printf("%s %d\n",s,add(x,2));
    return 0;
}
```

## One-line structs, enums, unions

`@s` declares a struct, `@u` a union and `@e` an enum, each with its typedef. Fields are `names:type` (`*T` for pointers), inline separated by `;` or as an indented block.

```nanoc
@s Point x,y:f64
@s Node
  val:i32
  next:*Node
@e Color red,green=5,blue
@f main int
  Point p={1,2}
  Node n={3,NULL}
  Color c=blue
  p.x+p.y!=3 || n.val!=3 || c!=6
```

```c
typedef struct Point Point;
struct Point {
    double x,y;
};

typedef struct Node Node;
struct Node {
    int val;
    Node *next;
};

typedef enum {
    red,
    green=5,
    blue
} Color;

int main(void) {
    Point p={1,2};
    Node n={3,NULL};
    Color c=blue;
    return p.x+p.y!=3 || n.val!=3 || c!=6;
}
```

## Printing, imports and escape hatch

`say a, b` prints values separated by spaces with a newline; formats come from the C11 `_Generic` type of each value. `say` adds `stdio.h` itself. `@use a, b` includes several headers at once, `@use "mine"` is a local `mine.h`, and bundles expand to many: `std` (stdio, stdlib, string), `libc`, `posix`, `cxx`. In C++ the standard headers lose their `.h`: `@use vector`. An indented `@c` block is copied to the C output untouched, for anything NanoC lacks. `--std c89|c99|c11|c17` restricts the output: `i64` becomes `long` in c89 and `say` of values needs c11.

```nanoc
@c
  static int twice(int x) { return x*2; }
@f main int
  say "twice", twice(21), 1.5
  0
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

static int twice(int x) {
    return x*2;
}

int main(void) {
    {
        fputs("twice", stdout);
        putchar(' ');
        printf(_Generic((twice(21)), char *: "%s", const char *: "%s", float: "%g", double: "%g",
                long double: "%Lg", char: "%c", unsigned char: "%u", unsigned short: "%u", unsigned: "%u",
                long: "%ld", unsigned long: "%lu", long long: "%lld", unsigned long long: "%llu",
                default: "%d"), twice(21));
        putchar(' ');
        printf(_Generic((1.5), char *: "%s", const char *: "%s", float: "%g", double: "%g",
                long double: "%Lg", char: "%c", unsigned char: "%u", unsigned short: "%u", unsigned: "%u",
                long: "%ld", unsigned long: "%lu", long long: "%lld", unsigned long long: "%llu",
                default: "%d"), 1.5);
        putchar('\n');
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## Cleanup that cannot be forgotten

`defer stmt` runs the statement when its block ends and before every `ret` after it, last deferred first. A returned value is computed before the cleanup runs.

```nanoc
@use stdio
@f work(int fail) int
  puts("open")
  defer puts("close")
  if fail
    ret 7
  3
@f main int = work(1)!=7
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int work(int fail) {
    puts("open");
    {
        if (fail) {
            {
                int nanoc_ret_1 = (7);
                puts("close");
                return nanoc_ret_1;
            }
        }
        {
            int nanoc_ret_2 = (3);
            puts("close");
            return nanoc_ret_2;
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    return work(1)!=7;
}
```

## Switch without the noise

`match x` takes arms of comma-separated values with an indented body, and `else` for the default. No `break`, no fallthrough. It becomes a plain C `switch`.

```nanoc
@f size(int x) int
  r:=0
  match x
    1, 2
      r=10
    else
      r=-1
  r
@f main int = size(2)!=10 || size(9)!=-1
```

```c
int size(int x) {
    int r = 0;
    switch (x) {
        case 1:
        case 2:
            {
                r=10;
            }
            break;
        default:
            {
                r=-1;
            }
            break;
    }
    return r;
}

int main(void) {
    return size(2)!=10 || size(9)!=-1;
}
```

## Inference and ranges

`:=` infers the type of a scalar literal. `for i 1..6` counts from 1 up to but not including 6.

```nanoc
#include <stdio.h>
@f main int
  total:=0
  for i 1..6
    total+=i
  printf("%d\n",total)
  0
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    int total = 0;
    {
        int nanoc_start_1 = (1);
        int nanoc_end_2 = (6);
        for (int i = nanoc_start_1; i < nanoc_end_2; ++i) {
            total+=i;
        }
    }
    printf("%d\n",total);
    return 0;
}
```

- Spell the type when you need it: `int x=call()`. C++ uses `auto` for `:=`.
- Typed range: `for i:usize 0..n`. Bounds are evaluated once.
- Plain C loops still work: `for int i=0;i<n;i++`. `loop` is `for (;;)`, `unless c` is `if !(c)`, `until c` is `while !(c)`.
- C++ iterates containers: `for value values`.
- Shortcuts: `nil` is NULL, `and`/`or`/`not` are `&&`/`||`/`!`, `@inc stdio, "mine.h", <sys/x.h>` includes headers (bare names become `<name.h>`).

## Token templates

`@m` defines a template. `$x` captures a token. A macro with `=` and no parameters is a named constant.

```nanoc
#include <stdio.h>
@m twice($x)
  (($x)*2)
@m answer = 42
@m maxfn($name,$type)
  @f $name($type a,b) $type = a>b?a:b
@maxfn(max_int,int)
@f main int
  printf("%d %d\n",@twice(@answer),max_int(2,3))
  0
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int max_int(int a, int b) {
    return a>b?a:b;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("%d %d\n", ((42)*2),max_int(2,3));
    return 0;
}
```

> Use `$fresh(tmp)` for generated names that must not collide. `$$` writes a literal `$`.

Captures: `$x` / `$x:tokens`, `$x:ident`, `$x:block`; a last `$xs...` is a list. Templates substitute `$x`, `$($xs),*`, `$fresh(tmp)`. An `=` selects a program: its last expression returns text, tokens, numbers or bools, or it can emit code. A final `$body:block` argument can be an indented body after the call.

## Generate code with `@ct`

An indented `@ct` block runs during expansion. `emit` writes NanoC back into the source, so you can generate functions in a loop.

```nanoc
#include <stdio.h>
@ct
  f square(n) = n*n
  for i 1..5
    emit("@f square_"+str(i)+" int = "+str(square(i))+"\n")
@f main int
  printf("%d\n",square_4())
  0
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int square_1(void) {
    return 1;
}

int square_2(void) {
    return 4;
}

int square_3(void) {
    return 9;
}

int square_4(void) {
    return 16;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("%d\n",square_4());
    return 0;
}
```

Programs use int64, bool, text, tokens and lists. Bind `x:=expr`, assign `x=expr`; controls are indented: `for i range(n)`, `if cond`, `while cond`. Functions are `f name(args) = expr` or an indented final expression. `quote(C tokens)` interpolates `$name`, `ident(text)` builds names, `eval(read(path))` loads a program library.

CT and macros expand recursively. `source()` reads the current snapshot, `rewrite(text)` repeats only on changed text, `again()` forces another pass, `get`/`put` keep state.

## Files and commands with `@bt`

`@bt` is the only phase that may write files or run host commands. It runs first and is removed; the code it emits prefixes the input. Use `--check` to validate a file without side effects; it rejects these calls.

```nanoc
@bt
  mkdir("build")
  write("build/nanoc-generated.h","#define GENERATED 42\n")
  emit(read("build/nanoc-generated.h"))
@f main int = GENERATED!=42
```

```c
#define GENERATED 42

int main(void) {
    return GENERATED!=42;
}
```

`run(argv[,cwd])` returns `[status,out,err]`; `exec` returns stdout or fails; `sh` runs a shell line. Defaults: 32 passes, 1M steps, 16 MiB input/output, depth 128 (ceiling 512). `--max-passes 0 --max-steps 0` removes the count limits, not the other resource limits.

## Inline assembly

An indented `@asm` block forwards instructions to the GCC or Clang inline assembler, with explicit `out`, `in`, `clobber` and `labels` sections. Assembly is the only place NanoC knows a target; everything else is plain C.

Full syntax and examples: `nanoc --describe asm` or the [assembly card](https://github.com/mkalmousli/NanoC/blob/main/docs/assembly.md).

## C++17 and C headers

Headers work unchanged. Use `--lang c++` to emit C++17 and get range loops over standard containers. `--emit mini` strips comments and layout for the smallest C.

```nanoc
#include <vector>
#include <iostream>
@f main int
  values:=std::vector<int>(3,2)
  sum:=0
  for value values
    sum+=value
  std::cout<<sum<<'\n'
  0
```

> Build: `nanoc app.nc --lang c++ -o app.cc && c++ -std=c++17 app.cc -o app`

## Cheat sheet

| Syntax | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `@f name(args) T` | Function; bare return type; `= expr` for one line |
| `x:=expr` | Infer a local's type from a scalar literal |
| `for i a..b` | Range loop, exclusive upper bound |
| `if / elif / else` | Branches; as a final expression they return a value |
| `@m name($x) body` | Macro template; `$x` captures, `$fresh(t)` |
| `@ct` | Compile-time program; `emit` writes source |
| `@bt` | Build-time program; files and commands |
| `@asm` | Inline assembly block |

> CLI: `nanoc f.nc -o f.c` · `--check --diagnostics json` · `--lang c++` · `--describe syntax|builtins|asm`
